JOURNAL

Taipei at Night, My Most Frequent Collaborator

2026.09.16

If Yu Stellar had to list a set of collaborators, late-night Taipei would probably sit near the top. Not some romanticized idea of a city, but something very specific — the white light of a convenience store, the fading sound of a scooter engine, a single window still lit somewhere — all of it quietly turns into an image inside a song without anyone deciding it should.

Daytime Taipei is busy, busy enough that all the sounds stack on top of each other until you can't tell them apart. But late-night Taipei slowly peels the sounds apart — the traffic goes first, then the voices, until all that's left is wind, an air-conditioning unit humming outside, and the occasional taxi passing by. That filtered kind of quiet is the background Yu Stellar writes to most often.

Walking through streets like that late at night, there's sometimes a strange feeling of being awake alongside the whole city, with no one else aware of it. That loneliness doesn't actually feel sad — it feels more like being quietly kept company by the city itself, even though it never says a word.

So if a song you're listening to feels wide-open and quiet at once, that's probably late-night Taipei leaving its trace on it.
